Build Your Own Redis with C/C++

summary.title: Build Your Own Redis with C/C++
summary.one_liner: You learn to build a Redis-like key-value server from scratch in C/C++, covering socket networking, event loops, hashtables, sorted sets, TTL expiration and thread pools.
keywords: tcp server and client in c
takeaways: Build a TCP server and client with socket programming
Design a request-response protocol and concurrent IO models, including an event loop
Implement a key-value server with hashtables and data serialization
Implement balanced binary trees, sorted sets, timers, TTL cache expiration and a thread pool
Recommended supplementary reading: Beej's Guide to Network Programming, The Linux Programming Interface, and K&R's The C Programming Language
summary.summary: This free web book walks readers through building a Redis server from scratch, starting with socket programming and a TCP server/client, then a request-response protocol and concurrent IO models. It moves through an event loop and a key-value server, then advanced topics such as hashtables, serialization, balanced binary trees, sorted sets, timeouts, TTL cache expiration and thread pools. The author's stated approach is small, incremental steps that distill the core concepts of the much larger real Redis codebase. Source code is provided as a tarball, and the page recommends three supporting books on networking, Linux APIs and C.
